title: Kunneth formula, etale cohomology
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed
field and let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$.
Let $n\ge1$ be an integer invertible in $k$. Then for
$E\in D(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\kunZn)$ the
Kunneth map of [def-kun-kunneth-map]

$$
\kappa_{E,K}:\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. (*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F1P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1P).)

proof.text:
Write $a:X\to\Spec(k)$ and $b:Y\to\Spec(k)$ for the structure morphisms. Apply [lem-kun-0f1n] with $S'=\Spec(k)$, $T=Y$, $p=\operatorname{id}_X$, $f'=a$, $g=b$, $h=\pr_1$, $e=\pr_2$, and $F=K$, to the diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&X&\xleftarrow{\;\pr_1\;}&X\times_kY\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle \pr_2}\\
\Spec(k)&\xleftarrow{\;=\;}&\Spec(k)&\xleftarrow{\;b\;}&Y
\end{array}
$$

Both squares are cartesian, since $X\times_k\Spec(k)=X$ and the right square defines $X\times_kY$. The product is finite type: choose finite affine covers $\Spec A_i$ of $X$ and $\Spec B_j$ of $Y$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; the product charts have rings $A_i\otimes_kB_j$, generated by the two finite sets of generators. Thus every scheme in the diagram is finite type over $k$, and $n$ is invertible in $k$ as required. The product-square map $\varphi$ specified in [lem-kun-kunneth-via-0f1n] is this specialization of the canonical map of [lem-kun-0f1n], with the displayed constant-complex source. We obtain the isomorphism

$$
\varphi:
E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\underline{\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)}
\longrightarrow
R\pr_{1,*}\bigl(\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr).
$$

We first check the qcqs hypotheses used below. A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. The finite affine covers just described have Noetherian coordinate rings by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and their underlying spaces are Noetherian by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. Every open in such a chart is quasi-compact: a maximal finite union of members of any open cover exists by the ascending-chain condition and must equal the open being covered. Intersecting an open with the finitely many charts proves that every open in $X$ or $X\times_kY$ is quasi-compact. In particular $X$ is quasi-compact and its affine-open intersections are quasi-compact, so it is quasi-separated. The inverse image of every affine open of $X$ under $\pr_1$ is quasi-compact. For affine opens $U,V$ of $X\times_kY$ mapping into a common affine open $W$ of $X$, the inverse image of the affine open $U\times_W V$ under the relative diagonal is $U\cap V$, which is quasi-compact. These affine opens cover the relative product, so the diagonal is quasi-compact. Thus $\pr_1$ is qcqs. It is a $k$-morphism, so [lem-kun-0f10](1) gives $\kuncd(\pr_1)<\infty$.

We conclude by [lem-kun-kunneth-via-0f1n] and the following
two identifications: first,
$\RGamma((X\times_kY)_{\Et},-)\cong\RGamma(X_{\Et},-)\circ R\pr_{1,*}$
by [lem-kun-leray-unbdd], whose hypotheses were checked above; second,

$$
\RGamma\bigl(X_{\Et},E\kunotimes{\kunZn}\underline{\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)}\bigr)
\cong\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\kunZn}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
$$

by [lem-kun-0f12] with the torsion ring $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ and the arbitrary complex $\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)\in D(\Lambda)$. Here $X$ is qcqs as checked above and $\kuncd(X)<\infty$ by [lem-kun-0f10](2), which already incorporates the separably closed point calculation. The first arrow of the composite in [lem-kun-kunneth-via-0f1n] is precisely the canonical isomorphism of [lem-kun-0f12] (in the direction from the tensor of global sections); the second is $\RGamma(X_{\Et},\varphi)$ followed by the Leray identification. A functor sends an inverse of $\varphi$ to an inverse of its image, and the composite of these isomorphisms is an isomorphism. Hence $\kappa_{E,K}$ (the Kunneth map of
[def-kun-kunneth-map]) is an isomorphism, as desired.

lean.statement:
theorem isIso_kunnethMap_of_isSepClosed {W : Scheme.{u}} (p₁ : W ⟶ X) (p₂ : W ⟶ Y)
    (sq : IsPullback p₁ p₂ aX aY)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))) :
    IsIso (kunnethMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) p₁ p₂ aX aY (p₁ ≫ aX) rfl sq.w.symm E K)
lean.note: The live upstream source explicitly states blueprint thm-kun-0f1p for the same canonical kunnethMap recorded by def-kun-kunneth-map. Specialize its finite coefficient ring Λ to ULift.{u+1} (ZMod n) (the same ring under the canonical ULift ring equivalence, with module carriers in universe u+1); n ≥ 1 makes Λ finite, n annihilates Λ, and IsUnit (n : k) supplies HasInvertibleExponent Λ (Spec (.of k)). LocallyOfFiniteType plus QuasiCompact is exactly finite type. Take W to be the fibre product and sq its IsPullback witness. The conclusion is the node's canonical map in D((Spec k)_et, Λ); the separably closed point equivalence and the canonical Leray and tensor identifications give precisely the displayed map in D(Λ). The adjacent nonempty_iso_kunneth_of_isSepClosed constructs that identification by applying derived global sections to this very map; the attachment uses IsIso of the specified map, not a bare existence of an isomorphism. No duplicate theorem is written. Read using scompile.py --source, since the older local upstream checkout lacks this module.
